messages:
mira: Quick follow-up to the API v4 RFC — proposal to support a temporary server-side conversion for the old `body` -> new `payload` shape so tenants can migrate without immediate client changes. Looking for tradeoffs and a rollout plan.

sam: quick q — is the conversion lossy? any fields we can't roundtrip?

julian: Not inherently lossy. attachments -> payload.attachments, rename `ctx`->`context`. Some deprecated flags are dropped if missing in v4, but we can preserve them under `metadata` to be safe.

mira: Rough plan: gateway-level shim that, for opt-in tenants, converts incoming v3-shaped `body` into v4 `payload` for services, and converts responses back. Opt-in via header `X-RI-Compat: body-v3-to-v4` or tenant UI toggle. Pros: no client upgrades required. Cons: latency, more moving parts in gateway.

taylor: SDK polyfill still an option — push client libs to convert on the client side. That avoids runtime cost but depends on customers updating.

sam: performance numbers? curious about per-request overhead.

julian: In staging proto of the shim: parse+transform+serialize adds ~0.8–1.5ms avg per request. Worst-case (big attachments) higher. We can add a small LRU cache for identical payloads to shave some p99.

mira: Telemetry we need: `compat.hits` (by tenant), `compat.latency_ms`, `compat.error_count`, and `compat.signature_conflicts`. Also tag by route and model.

ops-bot: Canary plan suggestion — route to 3% traffic for 48h, alert if `compat.error_count / compat.hits > 0.05` or `compat.latency_ms.p95` increases by >30%.

taylor: Important edge: signed payloads/HMACs. Converting changes canonical representation and will break signatures.

sam: yeah — we shouldn't break signing. Options: 1) refuse conversion if `X-RI-Signed: true` and return 412 + migration instructions; 2) do transparent signature re-signing — but that's unacceptable for security.

mira: Agreed. Rule: if request contains `X-RI-Signed: true` or tenant has enforced signing, gateway should return 412 with a link to migration docs.

julian: Another alternative is a service-level adapter lib so each service does conversion. Pros: no gateway complexity; cons: duplication and harder to ensure parity.

taylor: Ops preference? central gateway is easier to control rollout, but we must make it robust and well-tested. Also request a feature flag to target only dedicated pools (so shared hosts are unaffected).

mira: Good point — add `compat.target_pool` flag to the toggle (shared|dedicated).

mira: Proposed rollout tasks: 1) Prototype shim in staging gateway (julian) 2) Implement telemetry counters + dashboard (sam) 3) Tenant opt-in toggle + UI + docs (taylor) 4) Migration docs + deprecation timeline (mira) — suggest 6 months with weekly reminders.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll wire metrics and a basic dashboard.

julian: I'll push a prototype branch with unit tests and a small benchmark. Pseudo-converter: ```python
def convert_body_v3_to_v4(body_v3):
    payload = {}
    payload['text'] = body_v3.get('text')
    payload['attachments'] = [map_att(a) for a in body_v3.get('attachments', [])]
    payload['metadata'] = {k:v for k,v in body_v3.items() if k not in ('text','attachments')}
    return payload
```

taylor: One more ask: include a kill-switch at the gateway (feature flag + rollout circuit) and document failure modes in the runbook.

mira: Will add to runbook and RFC follow-up. If nobody objects to the header opt-in + tenant toggle approach I'll schedule a quick sync to finalize acceptance criteria.

taylor: No objections from me.

sam: No objections.

julian: OK from my side — will start prototype tomorrow.

mira: Thanks all — I'll create the follow-up meeting and a tracking issue with the action items.
